# Pre-registration — H40–H43, forward paper-trading engine

**Registered:** on the merge commit of this file. That commit's SHA and
timestamp are the durable record even if Supabase were lost.
**Engine under test:** `paper_engine/` (forward). **Reference engine:**
`experiments/cc_sim.py` + `cc_core.py` at `b3f55bd`.
**Reference data:** `reference.json`, regenerated by `derive_reference.py`.
**Thresholds:** `thresholds.json`, regenerated by `derive_thresholds.py`, and
embedded verbatim at the bottom of this file.

**This document is immutable.** Its SHA-256 is stored in each of H40–H43's
`signal_graveyard.pass_thresholds` at registration time, and the engine
recomputes and compares it before every single decision. Editing anything here
— a threshold, a date, a caveat that turns out to be inconvenient — changes the
hash and stops the engine. There is no cosmetic-edit exemption, because
deciding what counts as cosmetic is exactly the discretion this removes. To
change a rule: stop the study, register a new hypothesis, start a new clock,
and report the two separately forever.

Every number below is either **derived** (arithmetic shown, regenerable from a
committed script) or explicitly labelled **arbitrary starting value**. Nothing
is presented as measured that was chosen.

---

## 1. The arms

All four run simultaneously, on the same tickers, the same daily entry
evaluations, the same captured quotes. They differ ONLY in which decisions they
act on. A quote missing for one arm is missing for all.

| Arm | Hypothesis | Entry gate | Exits | Isolates |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A — full strategy | **H40** | per-ticker IV-rank threshold (DIS ≥ 75, else 50) + shared liquidity floor | full copilot ladder | the product as shipped |
| B — hold to expiry | **H41** (as A−B) | identical to A | none; settle at expiry, modelled rational early exercise still applies | the copilot's entire value and cost |
| C — no IV gate | **H42** | liquidity floor only | identical to A | the IV gate's forward value |
| D — take-profit only | **H43** (as A−D) | identical to A | acts only on `close_soon_tp75` and `emergency_itm_exdiv_3d` | how much of A's exit cost is defensive vs profit-taking |

Universe: the non-skip production tickers at registration — **AAPL, DIS, GOOGL,
KKR, TMUS**. Sizing: `get_max_contracts(ticker, 10_000)`, KKR capped at 7
contracts by the Exp 021 liquidity cap.

Fills are executable-conservative and always will be: **sell at the bid, buy
back at the ask**, at the first tick at or after decision + 15 minutes,
commission $0.65/contract/side charged as its own line. This bias runs in
exactly one direction and it is the safe one.

---

## 2. Epistemic contract — what may be claimed from what

| Claim source | Trust it for | Never trust it for |
|---|---|---|
| BSM / synthetic backfill (old `paper_trades`) | Nothing. Directional intuition at most. | Any deployment decision or published number |
| Backtest on Databento, **all fills** | Mechanism instrumentation — which clause fires, how often; relative comparisons where both sides share the same staleness | Absolute P&L or retention; any per-ticker sign below ~70% repricing coverage |
| Backtest on Databento, **real-fill subset** | Sign and rough magnitude per ticker; deriving the thresholds in this document | Precision beyond the coverage %; thin names (KKR at 67.5%) |
| **This engine, forward** | The only source that can ever justify "it works" — against these pre-registered thresholds, with stated sample sizes | Anything before the cycle floors in §4; crash-regime behaviour it has not lived through |

**It falsifies fast and confirms slowly.** A strategy that loses money over six
months of bid/ask fills with 15-minute latency is dead, and that verdict is
*stronger* than one from real trading, because these fills are strictly worse
than achievable. A positive result means "process-faithful, honestly measured,
positive in the regime we lived through" — not "edge proven". Six months is one
regime draw; half-year retention swings of −78%→+93% are on record for DIS.

Production settings, production IV gate, 25 staggered sequential chains.
**Real-fill subset is the result**; all-fill sits beside it and never replaces

| Ticker | Window | Cycles | Real-fill coverage | $/cycle real-fill | $/cycle all-fill | Retention (kept / collected) | Hold p50/p90 | Cycles/yr | Per-cycle win rate | Worst 30d drawdown |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TMUS | 2025-03-21…2026-03-20 | 89 | 78.8% | **$1.50** | $16.76 | 1.2% ($133 / $10,692) | 25/31d | 13.0 | 88.9% | $765 |
| KKR | 2023-03-21…2026-03-20 | 256 | 67.5% | **−$15.80** | $6.16 | −12.5% (−$4,044 / $32,295) | 22/31d | 16.7 | 71.0% | $374 |
| DIS | 2025-03-21…2026-03-20 | 37 | 77.1% | **$74.65** | $94.64 | 34.3% ($2,762 / $8,053) | 19/28d | 4.0 | 100.0% | $748 |
| AAPL | 2025-03-21…2026-03-20 | 89 | 98.9% | **$7.84** | $7.90 | 15.8% ($698 / $4,408) | 21/28d | 12.0 | 90.9% | $971 |

Stress window (2020-02…2020-09), real-fill: TMUS −$6.39/cycle (−4.5% retention),
KKR −$12.36 (−15.4%), DIS +$80.70 (+16.8%).

**Two windows are excluded and must never be quoted.** AAPL 2020 and GOOGL 2020
are **split-contaminated**: Databento strikes are as-traded, the proxy's stock
closes are split-adjusted, so across AAPL's 4:1 (2020-08-31) and GOOGL's 20:1
the strike ladder sits 4× and 20.7× above spot. Every call expires worthless and
the window reports spectacular retention — the first run of `derive_reference.py`
produced AAPL 2020 = **$13,731/cycle at 99.7% retention on 100% coverage**, which
is not a result but an artefact. `derive_reference.py` now refuses these windows
automatically (band [0.70, 1.50] on median strike / spot, derived from the clean
windows' observed 0.98–1.23 spread; rejects when >5% of days fall outside).

**GOOGL has no reference at all** — five trading days of recent Databento data.
It trades in every arm and its forward numbers are reported, but it is excluded
from every pre-registered verdict and has no calibrated kill threshold. Stated
here so nobody grades it later by improvising a rule.

### Arm scores in the reference (all-fill, recent window)

| Ticker | A net / assignments | B net / assignments | C net (n) | D net / assignments |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TMUS | $1,894 / **0** | $9,147 / **10** | $8,988 (231) | $4,865 / 5 |
| KKR | $2,335 / **0** | −$16,580 / **102** | −$1,222 (733) | −$8,578 / 64 |
| DIS | $4,543 / **0** | −$8,477 / **10** | $6,473 (229) | −$7,939 / 9 |
| AAPL | $711 / **0** | $4,424 / **0** | $2,659 (231) | $4,123 / 0 |

**Arm A took zero assignments in every window; arm B took 0–102.** Being called
away is the tax event the copilot exists to prevent, and option-leg P&L cannot
see it. Any A−B readout that omits both arms' assignment counts is a misreport,
and this document pre-commits to that being a reporting failure rather than a
finding.

## 4. Verdict rules — and what is honestly gradeable

Every rule is **(cycle floor) AND (bootstrap CI condition)**. Floors come from
`n ≥ (1.645·sd/|mean|)²` on the reference's own per-cycle distributions —
a normal-approximation power sketch on overlapping, autocorrelated cohorts, so
an order of magnitude rather than a promise. Minimum floor 10 (**arbitrary**,
so that no rule can be satisfied by three lucky cycles).

### Rules

- **H40** passes for a ticker iff completed real-fill cycles ≥ its floor AND
  the 90% bootstrap CI (10,000 resamples) of per-cycle net option-leg P&L
  excludes 0 above it; fails iff the CI excludes 0 below it; otherwise
  **INCONCLUSIVE**, which is a verdict and not a deferral.
- **H41** (A−B) concludes "the copilot adds value" iff paired cycles ≥ floor
  AND the 90% CI of per-cycle (A−B) excludes 0 in A's favour; "net-negative on
  the option leg" iff it excludes 0 against A. Always reported with both arms'
  assignment counts.
- **H42** (IV gate) is measured on the **blocked set** — the entries arm C
  takes and arm A does not. It is *not* a paired comparison: on days both arms
  enter, the trades are identical and the paired delta is exactly 0 by
  construction. Concludes "the gate destroys value" iff blocked entries ≥ floor
  AND the 90% CI of their per-cycle P&L excludes 0 above it.
- **H43** (A−D) concludes "the defensive clauses carry the exit cost" iff paired
  cycles ≥ floor AND the 90% CI of per-cycle (A−D) excludes 0; sign gives
  direction.

**Pairing key, pinned:** a "paired cycle" matches two arms' trades on the
**shared entry** — `(ticker, contract_symbol, entry_decision_ts)` — which is
identical across arms by construction. Never on `cycle_seq`, which is allocated
per (arm, ticker) and desynchronizes the moment arms exit at different times;
pairing on it compares unrelated cycles from different market paths exactly
when the arms diverge, which is the one moment pairing exists to measure. (The
first implementation made this mistake; a correctness review caught it on
2026-08-21, before registration.)

Rules are registered **per ticker**. Pooling across tickers is the wrong
estimator here and is reported as secondary only: the per-ticker A−B means have
opposite signs (TMUS −$64, AAPL −$41, KKR +$50, DIS +$271), so pooling cancels
them and the pooled requirement (270 cycles) is worse than every per-ticker one.

### The reachability table — pre-committed, not discovered at review time

Expected completed cycles by day 180, against each rule's floor:

| Ticker | Cycles by day 180 | H40 floor | H41 (A−B) floor | H42 (gate) floor | H43 (A−D) floor |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| AAPL | 5.9 | 794 | 42 | 61 | 50 |
| DIS | 2.0 | 23 | 14 | 415 | 15 |
| KKR | 8.2 | 360 | 119 | 502 | 258 |
| TMUS | 6.4 | **58,101** | **25** | **10** | 113 |

**Nothing in this study is gradeable at day 180.** The two closest are TMUS's
IV-gate question (floor 10 blocked entries) and TMUS's copilot question (floor
25 paired cycles against 6.4 expected). Everything else needs years.

Two things follow, and both are registered now rather than negotiated later:

1. **The spec's premise holds, per ticker.** Pairing does cancel regime noise
   exactly as claimed: the arm-difference questions need 14–258 cycles where the
   absolute-P&L question needs 23–58,101. TMUS is the extreme case — its mean is
   $1.50/cycle against a $121 standard deviation, so its absolute question needs
   ~58,000 cycles. That is not a defect in the rule; it is the measurement
   saying TMUS's edge, if it exists, is far smaller than its noise.
2. **Day 180 is an interim readout, not a verdict.** It reports point estimates
   and honest CIs, every one labelled under-powered, plus the falsification
   result — which *is* reachable, because a strategy losing money badly shows up
   long before a small positive edge can be confirmed.

The H42 floors count **blocked entries**, not cycles, and the reference counts
those in cohort mode (every day evaluated) while the engine only evaluates a
ticker while it is flat. The forward accrual rate for blocked entries is
therefore **not derivable** from this reference and must be measured at day 30
before anyone estimates a date for that verdict.

## 5. Kill switches — two classes, never conflated

**Engine-integrity pauses** — the data is bad. Entries stop, monitoring
continues, and **no strategy conclusion may be drawn from the affected period**.
A period paused for bad data contains no evidence, not evidence against.

| Switch | Threshold | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| Quote coverage, trailing 5 sessions | < 80% | **arbitrary** — no forward observation exists yet; re-derive at day 30 |
| Assessments run with no usable option quote | > 5% of ticks | **arbitrary** — above this, TP-75/TP-50 are effectively off and no exit result means anything |
| Carried-forward quotes in one run | ≥ 3 | **arbitrary**, warns only |
| Schema contract fail / graveyard unreadable / SQLite backend | any | hard stop before the first decision |

**Strategy kills** — entries halt in the affected arm/ticker, Charles is
alerted, the milestone review convenes early. A TRIGGERED kill **never edits
`ticker_strategies.py`**; production changes stay behind pre-registration →
walk-forward → approval gate → one variable per commit.

| Switch | Threshold | Derivation |
|---|---|---|
| 30-day option-leg drawdown, arm A, real-fill | AAPL $1,462 · DIS $1,133 · KKR $646 · TMUS $1,185 | (reference worst 30d + modelled forward friction) × 1.5. First two derived; the 1.5× is **arbitrary**, revisit at day 90 |
| Any modelled assignment in arm A | ≥ 1, halts that ticker | mechanical. Reported with the approach count — the reference saw only **8** approaches to the assignment branch (all KKR) in 8,458 observations, so a forward zero may mean the state was never reached |
| Consecutive losing cycles, arm A, real-fill | AAPL 3 · KKR 5 · TMUS 3 · **DIS disarmed** | binomial: smallest M with (N−M+1)·q^M < α, α = 5% split four ways. DIS's reference win rate is 100%, giving no loss rate to solve against — it stays disarmed rather than carrying an invented number |
| EMERGENCY verdicts in 30 days | ≥ 2 | Poisson(λ=0.031) gives E=1; floored at 2 because one EMERGENCY is the copilot working, and this switch is for a *cluster*. The maths above the floor is derived, the floor is **arbitrary** |

## 6. Milestones — decisions written before the data exists

**Day 30 — integrity checkpoint. NO strategy verdicts.** Pre-committed so that
nobody quotes day-30 P&L. Graded: quote coverage per ticker; stale-fill %;
clause-fire counts for all 14 rungs; the assessed-without-ask counter; zero
silent Nones; heartbeat record; and confirmation the workflow is still enabled
(GitHub auto-disables schedules). Also re-derives the quote-coverage threshold
and measures the blocked-entry accrual rate, both of which are unmeasurable
before go-live.

Reference clause-fire baseline for that audit (recent window, arm A):
`safe_default` and `close_soon_tp75` dominate everywhere; `close_now_itm`,
`close_soon_within_2pct_dte_ge7`, `watch_2to5pct_dte_ge14` fire regularly;
`emergency_itm_exdiv_3d` fired **8 times, KKR only**;
`close_now_within_2pct_earnings_2d` and `watch_exdiv_5to10d_within_5pct` fired
**zero times** — the earnings clause is structurally unreachable in the
backtest because `cc_sim` passes `earnings_date=None`, and the forward engine
*does* pass real earnings dates, so it is the one clause expected to move from
zero. A clause still at zero forward after hundreds of observations is presumed
unwired, not unlucky.

**Day 90 — attribution interim.** Per-ticker A−B, A−D and blocked-set readouts
with CIs, every one labelled against its floor from §4. Kill-switch board
review. Cycle counts vs the registered floors. Pre-committed decision: *if arm
A's per-cycle net P&L trails arm B's by more than the reference A−B mean for
that ticker AND the paired count has reached that ticker's floor, escalate to
Charles as "the copilot is net-negative forward on the option leg", with both
arms' assignment counts attached.* Per §4 no ticker is expected to reach its
floor by day 90; the pre-committed outcome in that case is "INCONCLUSIVE —
under-powered", stated plainly.

**Day 180 — interim verdict.** Each of H40–H43 graded pass / fail /
inconclusive against its registered rule, and `mark_result` written to the
graveyard for all four **including the inconclusives**. Reported per ticker, as
ranges across sub-windows, real-fill and all-fill side by side, with §2's
caveats attached verbatim. A pass is *evidence for* Dad's onboarding decision —
Charles's call, per the Phase-2 runbook — never an automatic promotion.

---

## 6a. Concurrent live trading — registered before it happens

The milestones grade **this study**, not permission to trade. Real trading may
begin whenever Charles and Dad decide (the Phase-2 runbook owns that call), and
the study remains valid while it happens, because the arms trade on captured
quotes and their own rules — nothing an arm does depends on what Dad does.
Registered now so none of this is improvised later:

- **The kill board is the live turn-it-off signal.** Arm A runs the production
  rules on real quotes at Dad's size; if a strategy kill TRIGGERS on arm A
  while Dad trades the same rules, that is the pre-registered signal to stop
  real trading and convene the review — from day one, not day 180.
- **Execution audit.** While Dad trades, his actual fills can be compared
  against arm A's conservative fills (sell-at-bid, buy-at-ask, +15 min) on the
  same days. Arm A's fills are a floor by construction; Dad filling
  consistently WORSE than the floor is an execution problem the study must
  hear about. (A read-only "arm R" join of real `trades` rows into the health
  page is a follow-up, not part of this registration.)
- **Reflexivity caveat, KKR.** Dad's real orders at 7 contracts against a
  3-contract median daily volume can move the very quotes the engine captures.
  On thin names, forward results collected while Dad trades the same strike
  are partially reflexive and are flagged as such in every readout. Liquid
  names (AAPL, GOOGL, TMUS, DIS) are unaffected at his size.
- **No loosening either way.** Early live P&L — good or bad — changes no
  production parameter and no registered threshold; the walk-forward +
  approval-gate pipeline still owns every parameter change.

---

## 7. Known limitations, registered up front

- **The forward real-fill definition is STRICTER than the backtest's.** The
  reference table's real-fill subset is cc_sim's: the *exit* was priced by a
  real observation. The forward engine additionally excludes cycles whose
  *entry* filled on a carried-forward quote, settlements booked after expiry
  day (a later session's spot can fabricate or erase an assignment), and
  post-session fallback exits. Restricting only shrinks the graded subset —
  a forward real-fill number can be compared against the reference knowing
  the forward bar is higher, never lower.
- **Six months is one regime draw.** The 2020 stress windows remain the only
  crash evidence, they are real-fill-subset backtests rather than forward
  results, and two of the five tickers have no usable stress window at all.
- **The IV-rank definitions do not match.** The forward engine gates on the
  production number (`db.get_real_iv_rank`, falling back to the realized-vol
  proxy); the reference gates on `cc_sim.compute_iv_rank`, which is Exp 009's
  ATM-call-price definition. A−C is internally valid because both arms use the
  same function, but the forward IV-gate result is **not** directly comparable
  to the backtest's. Adding a fourth definition would make this worse, so it is
  recorded rather than fixed.
- **Assignment is modelled, never observed.** A paper position cannot be
  assigned. Every modelled assignment carries its full inputs and a `modeled`
  label.
- **CLOSE_SOON's clock is 5 calendar days**, from the alert's own wording
  ("Close this week") — not 5 trading days. `cc_core` is the single definition
  and the simulator has always computed it this way.
- **The commission rate is an assumption** ($0.65/contract/side), not Dad's
  actual rate. Reported as its own line so it can be re-costed without
  re-running anything.
- **Real order-book impact is invisible** at these sizes except on KKR, which
  is what the 7-contract cap is for. Dad's actual behaviour under stress is
  also outside what this can measure.
